---
title: "Read 5' completeness and the cap (untemplated-G) signature: PBMC vs ALS"
output: github_document
---

Measurement only, to review before any change to LRAA's TSS calling. In ALS cortex nuclei,
most high-confidence TSS switches have a neuron cluster favouring a downstream TSS, and the
reads of housekeeping genes rarely reach the TSS (`ALS_LRAA_eval/__TSS_Truncation_Check`).
This report asks:

- **A.** How 5' completeness falls with distance from the 3' end, globally and per cluster.
- **B.** How much of the variation is per cluster and how much per gene.
- **C.** Whether the untemplated-G signature that template switching leaves at a capped 5' end
  separates reads that start at a TSS from reads that start inside a transcript body.
- **D.** What a completeness-aware degradation threshold would do to the high-confidence TSS
  events of each dataset.

Tables: `util/sc/tss_5prime_completeness.py` (LRAA), via the `Makefile` here. Reads are taken
with LRAA's read filters and transcribed-strand rule. Each read's 5' clip, and whether LRAA
strips it as untemplated G's, come from LRAA's `Pretty_alignment`. The exact rules are in the
script's header and in `README.md`.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 10, dpi = 120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(data.table); library(lme4); library(patchwork) })
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
```

## A. 5' completeness curves

For each gene and group of cells, S(d) is the share of its polyA-anchored reads whose 5'
extent from the 3' end is at least d nt, for d up to the gene's length L. Reads starting
within 50 nt of the TSS count as full length. K(d) is the mean of S(d) over genes with
L >= d and at least 20 anchored reads in that group, so each gene counts once whatever its
expression. Groups are a whole dataset, a cell-type class, or a cluster.

```{r curves}
grid = seq(0, 6000, by = 25)
gene_survival = function(group_cols) {
    # per gene x group: anchored reads n, reaching r; S(d) = (r + non-reaching reads with
    # bin >= d) / n for d on the grid up to the gene's length
    tot = ext[, .(n = sum(n_anchored), r = sum(n_reach), L = L[1]), by = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols)][n >= 20]
    h = hist[, .(n = sum(n)), by = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols, "bin")]
    hc = h[order(-bin), .(bin, cum = cumsum(n)), by = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols)][order(bin)]
    pts = tot[, .(d = grid[grid <= L]), by = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols)]
    pts = merge(pts, tot, by = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols))
    pts[, bin := d]
    # cum at the smallest bin >= d: a backward rolling join on bin
    pts[, cum := hc[pts, on = c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols, "bin"), roll = -Inf, x.cum]]
    pts[is.na(cum), cum := 0]
    pts[, S := (r + cum) / n]
    pts[, c("dataset", "gene_key", group_cols, "d", "n", "r", "L", "S"), with = FALSE]
}
ext[, all := "all"]
hist = merge(hist, ext[, .(dataset, gene_key, cluster, class, all)], by = c("dataset", "gene_key", "cluster"))
S_all = gene_survival("all")
S_class = gene_survival("class")
S_cluster = gene_survival("cluster")
K = function(S, group_cols) S[, .(K = mean(S), genes = .N), by = c("dataset", group_cols, "d")][genes >= 20]
K_all = K(S_all, "all"); K_class = K(S_class, "class"); K_cluster = K(S_cluster, "cluster")
K_cluster[, class := cls(dataset, cluster), by = dataset]

ggplot(K_all, aes(d, K, color = dataset)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 4000), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "distance from the 3' end, d (nt)", y = "K(d): share of molecules reaching d", title = "Whole dataset")
```

```{r curves_class, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(K_class, aes(d, K, color = factor(class, levels = class_order))) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ dataset) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 4000), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "d (nt from the 3' end)", y = "K(d)", color = NULL, title = "By cell-type class")
```

## B. Cluster vs gene: where the variation is

Per gene and cluster (at least 50 anchored reads): observed share reaching the TSS against
the share predicted by the cluster's curve at the gene's length, K_cluster(L).

```{r per_gene}
kc = K_cluster[, .(dataset, cluster, d, K)]
gc_tab = ext[, .(n = sum(n_anchored), r = sum(n_reach)), by = .(dataset, gene_key, cluster, class, L, gc100, first_exon_len, n_fit_reads)][n >= 50]
gc_tab[, dL := pmin(round(L / 25) * 25, max(grid))]
gc_tab = merge(gc_tab, kc, by.x = c("dataset", "cluster", "dL"), by.y = c("dataset", "cluster", "d"), all.x = TRUE)
gc_tab[, obs := r / n]
ggplot(gc_tab[!is.na(K)], aes(K, obs)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) + geom_abline(color = "red") +
    facet_wrap(~ dataset) + labs(x = "predicted from the cluster's curve, K_cluster(L)", y = "observed share reaching the TSS")
knitr::kable(gc_tab[!is.na(K), .(gene_clusters = .N, genes = uniqueN(gene_key),
                                 cor_pred_obs = cor(qlogis(pmin(pmax(K, 1e-3), 1 - 1e-3)), qlogis(pmin(pmax(obs, 1e-3), 1 - 1e-3))),
                                 median_abs_err = median(abs(obs - K))), by = dataset], digits = 3)
```

**Variance decomposition.** A binomial GLM of the per gene x cluster reach counts, adding
terms in turn: log(L), then cluster, then gene. The table gives each term's share of the
null deviance and what is left over. The residual is the gene x cluster interaction plus
binomial noise; its ratio to the residual degrees of freedom shows how much is beyond
binomial noise.

```{r decomp}
# additive logit model gene + cluster, fitted by alternating one-dimensional Newton updates
# (a glm with thousands of gene dummies is too slow); log(L) is constant within a gene, so
# the gene terms absorb it
fit_gene_cluster = function(d, iters = 50) {
    a = setNames(rep(0, uniqueN(d$gene_key)), unique(d$gene_key)); b = setNames(rep(0, uniqueN(d$cluster)), unique(d$cluster))
    upd = function(grp, eta_other, r, n, cur) {
        for (k in 1:5) {
            p = plogis(cur[grp] + eta_other)
            g = tapply(r - n * p, grp, sum); h = tapply(n * p * (1 - p), grp, sum)
            cur[names(g)] = cur[names(g)] + g / pmax(h, 1e-9)
        }
        cur
    }
    for (i in 1:iters) {
        a = upd(d$gene_key, b[d$cluster], d$r, d$n, a)
        b = upd(d$cluster, a[d$gene_key], d$r, d$n, b)
    }
    p = pmin(pmax(plogis(a[d$gene_key] + b[d$cluster]), 1e-12), 1 - 1e-12)
    -2 * sum(dbinom(d$r, d$n, p, log = TRUE) - dbinom(d$r, d$n, pmin(pmax(d$r / d$n, 1e-12), 1 - 1e-12), log = TRUE))
}
decomp = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) {
    d = gc_tab[dataset == ds]
    f0 = glm(cbind(r, n - r) ~ 1, binomial, d)
    f1 = glm(cbind(r, n - r) ~ log(L), binomial, d)
    f2 = glm(cbind(r, n - r) ~ log(L) + cluster, binomial, d)
    fc = glm(cbind(r, n - r) ~ cluster, binomial, d)
    d3 = fit_gene_cluster(d)
    dev = c(deviance(f0), deviance(f1), deviance(f2), d3)
    df3 = nrow(d) - uniqueN(d$gene_key) - uniqueN(d$cluster) + 1
    data.table(dataset = ds, term = c("log(L)", "+ cluster", "+ gene (beyond its length)", "residual (gene x cluster)"),
               share_of_null_deviance = c(-diff(dev), dev[4]) / dev[1],
               cluster_alone = c(NA, (deviance(f0) - deviance(fc)) / dev[1], NA, NA),
               resid_dev_per_df = c(NA, NA, NA, d3 / df3))
}))
knitr::kable(decomp, digits = 3)

```

```{r mixed}
fits = lapply(DS, function(ds) {
    d = gc_tab[dataset == ds]
    glmer(cbind(r, n - r) ~ scale(log(L)) + cluster + (1 | gene_key), family = binomial, data = d,
          control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
})
names(fits) = DS
mix = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) {
    fit = fits[[ds]]; ce = fixef(fit)[grepl("^cluster", names(fixef(fit)))]
    data.table(dataset = ds, `gene SD (logit)` = sqrt(VarCorr(fit)$gene_key[1]),
               `cluster range (logit, max - min)` = diff(range(c(0, ce))),
               `length effect per SD of log L (logit)` = unname(fixef(fit)[2]))
}))
knitr::kable(mix, digits = 2, caption = "Mixed model: reach ~ log(L) + cluster + (1 | gene)")

re = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) {
    r = ranef(fits[[ds]])$gene_key
    data.table(dataset = ds, gene_key = rownames(r), gene_effect = r[, 1])
}))
feat = merge(re, use[, .(dataset, gene_key, L, gc100, first_exon_len, n_fit_reads)], by = c("dataset", "gene_key"))
feat_cor = feat[, .(`GC of first 100 nt` = cor(gene_effect, gc100, method = "spearman", use = "complete"),
                    `log length` = cor(gene_effect, log(L), method = "spearman"),
                    `first exon length` = cor(gene_effect, first_exon_len, method = "spearman"),
                    `log reads (expression)` = cor(gene_effect, log(n_fit_reads), method = "spearman")), by = dataset]
knitr::kable(feat_cor, digits = 2, caption = "Spearman correlation of the per-gene effect (higher = reaches the TSS more often than its length and cluster predict) with gene features")
```

```{r gene_effect_consistency, fig.height = 4}
both = dcast(re, gene_key ~ dataset, value.var = "gene_effect")[!is.na(ALS) & !is.na(PBMC)]
ggplot(both, aes(PBMC, ALS)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6) + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "per-gene effect in PBMC (logit)", y = "per-gene effect in ALS (logit)",
         title = sprintf("Same genes in both datasets (n = %d): Spearman %.2f", nrow(both),
                         cor(both$PBMC, both$ALS, method = "spearman")))
```

## C. The untemplated-G (cap) signature

What the reads carry at their 5' ends (transcript orientation), on a sample of chr12 reads:

- **PBMC:** 66% have no clip and 25% a 1-base clip. Among clipped reads the proximal base is
  mostly a single G (about 42k of 66k); the next most common is a single A.
- **ALS:** 79% have no clip and 11% a 1-base clip. That clip is mostly a single A (about 13.5k)
  and less often a single G (about 5.9k).

LRAA strips a whole clip of 1-3 G's, or a proximal run of at least 3 G's, as untemplated G's
(`clip = G` below). An untemplated G aligns when the genome itself has a G just upstream of
the start, so it leaves no clip there. Signature rates are therefore given separately for
reads whose upstream genomic base is G (`upstream_G = 1`) and is not.

```{r capsig}
cap = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) fread(paste0(ds, ".capsig.tsv.gz"))[, dataset := ds]))
cap = cap[use[, .(dataset, gene_key)], on = .(dataset, gene_key), nomatch = 0]
cap[, class := cls(dataset, cluster), by = dataset]
cap[, five_class := factor(five_class, levels = c("TSS", "near", "body"))]
tab = cap[, .(reads = sum(reads)), by = .(dataset, upstream_G, five_class, clip)]
tab[, share := reads / sum(reads), by = .(dataset, upstream_G, five_class)]
knitr::kable(dcast(tab, dataset + upstream_G + five_class ~ clip, value.var = "share")[order(dataset, upstream_G, five_class)],
             digits = 3, caption = "Share of reads by 5' clip class. TSS: starts within 50 nt of the gene's TSS; near: 50-100 nt downstream; body: > 100 nt downstream")
grate = cap[upstream_G == 0, .(G_rate = sum(reads[clip == "G"]) / sum(reads), reads = sum(reads)),
            by = .(dataset, class, five_class)]
ggplot(grate[five_class != "near"], aes(factor(class, levels = class_order), G_rate, fill = five_class)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge") + facet_wrap(~ dataset, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "share of reads with a G signature (upstream base not G)", fill = "read starts at",
         title = "G signature: reads starting at the TSS vs inside the transcript body") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r capsig_gene, fig.height = 4.5}
pg = cap[upstream_G == 0 & five_class != "near", .(G = sum(reads[clip == "G"]), n = sum(reads)),
         by = .(dataset, gene_key, five_class)][n >= 20]
pgw = dcast(pg[, .(dataset, gene_key, five_class, rate = G / n)], dataset + gene_key ~ five_class, value.var = "rate")[!is.na(TSS) & !is.na(body)]
ggplot(pgw, aes(body, TSS)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.6) + geom_abline(color = "red") +
    facet_wrap(~ dataset) + coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "G-signature rate, reads starting in the body", y = "G-signature rate, reads starting at the TSS",
         title = "Per gene (>= 20 reads of each kind, upstream base not G)")
knitr::kable(pgw[, .(genes = .N, median_TSS = median(TSS), median_body = median(body),
                     share_genes_TSS_higher = mean(TSS > body)), by = dataset], digits = 2)
```

### At the high-confidence TSS events' sites

The same signature for reads starting within 25 nt of each event's upstream (U) and
downstream (D) site, pooled over clusters, for reads whose upstream base is not G. Within a
25 nt window the upstream base varies from read to read, so most sites have enough such reads.

```{r event_sites}
evs = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) {
    f = c(PBMC = "../../../LRAA_paper-PBMCs_study/__Site_Usage_Analysis/PBMCs.TSS_events_vs_CAGE.events.tsv",
          ALS = "../../../LRAA_paper-FTD_study/__Site_Usage_Analysis/LP00714.TSS_events_vs_CAGE.events.tsv")[ds]
    fread(f)[high_confidence == TRUE][, dataset := ds]
}), fill = TRUE)
evs[, down := gained_is_downstream == TRUE]
evs[, `:=`(U_site = fifelse(down, lost_site, gained_site), D_site = fifelse(down, gained_site, lost_site),
           D_A = fifelse(down, gained_reads_A, lost_reads_A), D_B = fifelse(down, gained_reads_B, lost_reads_B),
           U_A = fifelse(down, lost_reads_A, gained_reads_A), U_B = fifelse(down, lost_reads_B, gained_reads_B))]
evs[, `:=`(shD_A = D_A / (D_A + U_A), shD_B = D_B / (D_B + U_B))]
evs[, `:=`(fav = fifelse(shD_B >= shD_A, cluster_B, cluster_A), oth = fifelse(shD_B >= shD_A, cluster_A, cluster_B))]
evs[, fav_class := cls(dataset, fav), by = dataset]

es = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) fread(paste0(ds, ".event_sites.tsv.gz"))[, dataset := ds]))
srate = es[upstream_G == 0, .(G_rate = sum(reads[clip == "G"]) / sum(reads), n = sum(reads)), by = .(dataset, site_id)]
ev_sites = unique(evs[, .(dataset, gene_key, gene_symbol, U_site, D_site)])
ev_sites = merge(ev_sites, srate[, .(dataset, U_site = site_id, U_G = G_rate, U_n = n)], by = c("dataset", "U_site"), all.x = TRUE)
ev_sites = merge(ev_sites, srate[, .(dataset, D_site = site_id, D_G = G_rate, D_n = n)], by = c("dataset", "D_site"), all.x = TRUE)
ggplot(ev_sites[U_n >= 20 & D_n >= 20], aes(U_G, D_G)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + geom_abline(color = "red") +
    facet_wrap(~ dataset) + coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "G-signature rate at the upstream site", y = "at the downstream site",
         title = "High-confidence TSS events: site pairs (>= 20 reads at each, upstream base not G)")
knitr::kable(ev_sites[U_n >= 20 & D_n >= 20, .(site_pairs = .N, median_U = median(U_G), median_D = median(D_G),
                                               share_D_lower = mean(D_G < U_G)), by = dataset], digits = 2)
```

## D. A completeness-aware degradation threshold, simulated on the existing events

Suppose every molecule of a gene started at the upstream site U. A read would still start in
the 50 nt window around the downstream site D whenever the molecule's read stops there. In
cluster c, the expected number of such reads per read that reaches U is

  r_c = (K_c(d_D - 25) - K_c(d_D + 25)) / K_c(d_U)

where d_U and d_D are the distances of U and D from the 3' end, taken as the median aligned
distances of the reads that start at U, and K_c is cluster c's curve from A. This applies
only when D lies inside the molecules that start at U: at least half of the U-start reads
have D in an aligned exon. Otherwise a truncated U molecule cannot start at D, and the event
is exempt (AIF1-type alternative first exons).

Two rules, on the cluster where D's share of the U + D reads is higher (`fav`):

- **flag 1, truncation-consistent:** D_fav <= 2 x U_fav x r_fav. Then at least half of D's
  reads could be truncated U molecules. This is the completeness-aware analogue of LRAA's
  fixed `max_frac_alt_TSS_from_degradation = 0.20`.
- **flag 2, corrected shift:** subtract the expected truncation reads, D'_c = max(0, D_c - U_c r_c),
  and recompute D's share in both clusters. Flag if the corrected shift is < 0.2, or less than
  half the observed U-vs-D shift.

Not assessable: K_c(d_U) < 0.02, where the curve is too thin to divide by.

```{r simulate}
pairs = rbindlist(lapply(DS, function(ds) fread(paste0(ds, ".event_pairs.tsv"))[, dataset := ds]))
evs = merge(evs, pairs[, .(dataset, gene_key, U_site, D_site, D_in_U_body, d_U, d_D, U_start_reads)],
            by = c("dataset", "gene_key", "U_site", "D_site"), all.x = TRUE)
kfun = function(ds, cl, d) {
    k = K_cluster[dataset == ds & cluster == cl]
    if (!nrow(k) || is.na(d)) return(NA_real_)
    approx(k$d, k$K, xout = pmax(0, d), rule = 2)$y
}
simulate = function(factor = 2, min_shift = 0.2) {
    e = copy(evs)
    e[, applicable := !is.na(D_in_U_body) & D_in_U_body >= 0.5 & !is.na(d_U) & !is.na(d_D)]
    e[, c("KU_A", "KU_B", "w_A", "w_B") := {
        list(mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_A, d_U), mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_B, d_U),
             mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_A, d_D - 25) - mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_A, d_D + 25),
             mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_B, d_D - 25) - mapply(kfun, dataset, cluster_B, d_D + 25))
    }]
    e[, `:=`(r_A = pmax(w_A, 0) / KU_A, r_B = pmax(w_B, 0) / KU_B)]
    e[, assessable := applicable & pmin(KU_A, KU_B) >= 0.02]
    e[, `:=`(r_fav = fifelse(fav == cluster_B, r_B, r_A), D_fav = fifelse(fav == cluster_B, D_B, D_A),
             U_fav = fifelse(fav == cluster_B, U_B, U_A))]
    e[, flag1 := assessable & D_fav <= factor * U_fav * r_fav]
    e[, `:=`(Dc_A = pmax(0, D_A - U_A * r_A), Dc_B = pmax(0, D_B - U_B * r_B))]
    e[, `:=`(shDc_A = Dc_A / (Dc_A + U_A), shDc_B = Dc_B / (Dc_B + U_B))]
    e[, obs_shift := abs(shD_B - shD_A)]
    e[, corr_shift := fifelse(fav == cluster_B, shDc_B - shDc_A, shDc_A - shDc_B)]
    e[, flag2 := assessable & (corr_shift < min_shift | corr_shift < 0.5 * obs_shift)]
    e[, outcome := fcase(!applicable, "exempt (D not in U molecules)", !assessable, "not assessable",
                         flag1 | flag2, "flagged", default = "retained")]
    e[]
}
sim = simulate()
out = sim[, .(events = .N, genes = uniqueN(gene_key)), by = .(dataset, outcome)][order(dataset, outcome)]
knitr::kable(out, caption = "High-confidence TSS events under the simulated threshold (factor 2, corrected shift 0.2)")
knitr::kable(sim[, .(flag1 = sum(flag1, na.rm = TRUE), flag2 = sum(flag2, na.rm = TRUE),
                     both = sum(flag1 & flag2, na.rm = TRUE), assessable = sum(assessable, na.rm = TRUE)), by = dataset],
             caption = "Which rule flags")
sens = rbindlist(lapply(c(1.5, 2, 3), function(f) simulate(factor = f)[, .(factor = f, flagged = sum(outcome == "flagged"),
                                                                           events = .N), by = dataset]))
knitr::kable(dcast(sens, dataset + events ~ factor, value.var = "flagged"), caption = "Flagged events by the flag-1 factor")
```

```{r simulate_who}

           by = .(monocyte_favours_downstream = fav_class == "Monocyte / DC")]
knitr::kable(mono, caption = "PBMC: events where a monocyte / DC cluster favours the downstream site")
```

### For comparison: a cap-signature rule at the event sites

The same events, classified by the G signature alone. "D uncapped-like" means the
downstream site's G-signature rate is under a quarter of the upstream site's (at least 20
reads each, upstream base not G). This is not part of the completeness threshold above.

```{r cap_rule}
capr = merge(sim, ev_sites[, .(dataset, U_site, D_site, U_G, U_n, D_G, D_n)], by = c("dataset", "U_site", "D_site"), all.x = TRUE)
capr[, capclass := fcase(is.na(D_n) | D_n < 20 | is.na(U_n) | U_n < 20, "too few reads",
                         D_G < 0.25 * U_G, "D uncapped-like", default = "D capped-like")]
knitr::kable(capr[, .(events = .N, genes = uniqueN(gene_key), no_CAGE_peak_at_a_site = mean(cage == "no CAGE peak at a site"),
                      CAGE_assessable = sum(cage %in% c("agrees", "disagrees")),
                      CAGE_agree = mean(cage[cage %in% c("agrees", "disagrees")] == "agrees")),
                  by = .(dataset, capclass)][order(dataset, capclass)], digits = 2)
knitr::kable(capr[, .N, by = .(dataset, capclass, completeness_outcome = outcome)][order(dataset, capclass, completeness_outcome)],
             caption = "Cap-signature class vs the completeness threshold's outcome")
knitr::kable(unique(capr[gene_symbol %in% c("AIF1", "SELENOH", "EMP3"),
                         .(gene_symbol, U_site, D_site, U_G = round(U_G, 2), U_n, D_G = round(D_G, 2), D_n, capclass)]))
```

## Notes

- **Curves are means over genes, and only one TSS per gene is used.** A gene's own truncation
  can differ from its cluster's curve; section B measures by how much. The threshold in D
  uses only the cluster's curve.
- **Distances come from reads, so the threshold can't see positional hotspots.** d_U and d_D
  are aligned distances of the reads that start at U, which keeps the threshold independent of
  annotation. Truncation hotspots, where reads pile up at a specific position (for example
  ACTB near its 3' end), are not in a smooth curve. The threshold therefore under-predicts
  truncation at such positions.
- **Measurement only.** Nothing here changes LRAA's TSS calling or the site-usage results.
